title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page continues Grothendieck's historical survey (point g, the De Rham–Sullivan complex) for his 1976 IHÉS lecture on the De Rham complex with divided powers. It then begins a proof of Sullivan's De Rham theorem.

(1) Survey part. Sullivan showed that for simply connected X the rational homotopy type is recovered from the cochain algebra C*_DRS(X,Q). More precisely, Grothendieck adds 'sauf erreur' (barring error): C*_DRS gives an equivalence between:
- the weak homotopy category of connected, simply connected spaces; and
- a derived (homotopy) category of graded-commutative ('associatives et anticommutatives') differential graded Q-algebras A in degrees ≥0 with H^0(A)=Q and H^1(A)=0.

In modern terms these are 1-reduced CDGAs, localized at quasi-isomorphisms. There is a theory of minimal models for such algebras. From a minimal model (ΛV,d) one reads off π_i⊗Q very simply: V^i ≅ Hom(π_i(X),Q). Grothendieck's comment: 'Mais à nouveau, on perd la torsion!' (but again torsion is lost).

(2) Proof of the isomorphism H^q(C*_DRS/Q(X,Q)) ≅ H^q(X,Q).
- For each n, [n] is the standard simplex {Σx_i=1, x_i≥0}. Its realization is Δ^[n]_R, and E^[n] is the affine hyperplane Σx_i=1 in R^{n+1}, which carries a Q-structure.
- DRS_[n] = algebraic De Rham complex of E^[n] over Q, i.e. Q[x_0..x_n, dx_0..dx_n]/(Σx_i−1, Σdx_i). This is contravariant in [n], so DRS_* is a simplicial CDGA, which Grothendieck calls 'demi-simpliciale' and then corrects to simplicial. It is Sullivan's ∇(*,*), the polynomial forms on simplices.
- For any space X with singular simplicial set S_*(X): C*_DRS(X,Q) = Hom_{sSet}(S_*(X), DRS_*). In modern notation this is A_PL(X).

The next page completes the argument:
- Each DRS_* is a resolution of the constant Q (algebraic Poincaré lemma on the affine spaces E^[n]).
- Each component DRS^i_* is acyclic in the topos of simplicial sets (extendability / contractible Kan complex).
- Hence Hom(S_*X, −) computes H*(X,Q).

That page then explains why the naive Z-version fails (∫x^n dx needs 1/(n+1)), and proposes divided powers. The obstruction is that a simplex is an affine space, not a linear one, so it has no canonical origin for divided powers. This is the motivation for the lecture's title.
errors: Sullivan's equivalence as stated is too strong. It holds between the rational homotopy category (spaces localized at Q) of simply connected spaces, usually of finite Q-type, and minimal / 1-reduced CDGAs of finite type up to quasi-isomorphism. It is not an equivalence with the full weak homotopy category of simply connected spaces. Grothendieck's own 'sauf erreur' hedges this.
The algebras must be differential graded (CDGAs), not just graded algebras. This is implicit in 'catégorie dérivée' and in the conditions on H^0 and H^1.
'Demi-simpliciale' is self-corrected to simpliciale. The face maps alone suffice for the Hom formula, but DRS_* is genuinely simplicial.

ideas.what: Rational homotopy type of simply connected spaces is equivalent to the homotopy category of 1-reduced CDGAs over Q; minimal models give π_i⊗Q
ideas.modern_name: Sullivan rational homotopy theory, minimal models
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (Infinitesimal computations in topology, 1977; circulated c.1973-75); Quillen (1969) for the Lie side; Bousfield–Gugenheim (1976) for the model-category form
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (1983) discusses rational homotopy and schematization in a related spirit

ideas.what: Simplicial CDGA of polynomial forms on algebraic simplices; A_PL(X)=Hom(S_*X, ∇*); proof of the De Rham theorem via the Poincaré lemma plus acyclicity (extendability) of each degree
ideas.modern_name: Sullivan's polynomial De Rham forms A_PL; the 'extendable simplicial objects' argument

ideas.what: Remark that rational models lose torsion, motivating an integral De Rham–Sullivan theory (next page: via divided powers)
ideas.modern_name: Integral / p-adic algebraic models of homotopy types (E∞ cochains, binomial rings, schematization)

missed.claim: Already in 1976 Grothendieck frames the loss of torsion in Sullivan's theory as the key defect to fix. He aims at a functorial integral De Rham–Sullivan complex depending on X only through S_*(X), seven years before Pursuing Stacks' schematization program. The obstruction he isolates on the next page is that a simplex is an affine space without an origin, so divided powers are not canonical. Integer-valued (binomial) polynomials are precisely the affine-invariant replacement, and this is what Toën and Horel later used via cosimplicial binomial rings.
missed.quote: Mais à nouveau, on perd la torsion!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This dates Grothendieck's integral-homotopy-type program earlier than usually stated. The divided-power approach on simplices could be compared with the binomial-ring and derived-binomial-ring models, possibly yielding an explicit integral A_PL-type functor.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on this page is a standard exposition of Sullivan's theory and the A_PL De Rham theorem. The only notable point is historical: an early (1976) explicit motivation toward integral models through divided powers. That is partly known through mentions of the IHÉS lecture and is developed on the following pages.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the reading 'est récupéré à X' is doubtful; likely 'est récupérable à partir de' (via C*_DRS), with 'pour X simplement connexe' inserted above.
'(sauf erreur)' is an insertion above 'une équivalence'; 'faible' is inserted before 'des espaces connexes'.
'pour de telles algèbres' is the insertion above 'minimaux', replacing the struck 'une façon'.
In 'Algèbre différentielle graduée demi-simpliciale (cet = simpliciale)', the parenthetical reads 'cet = simpliciale' or similar, i.e. a self-correction to simplicial.
